instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines lobbying as communicating "directly or through his or her agents" with officials for the purpose of influencing legislative/administrative action without enumerating specific medium types (oral, written, electronic, etc.); it does not list specific activity types from the question's enumeration.

The statute requires registration of lobbying firms (including individual contract lobbyists/professional consultancies) under §82038.5 and lobbyist employers (covering in-house company and organisation lobbyists who employ lobbyists) under §82039.5; individual lobbyists are covered under §82039; §86300(a) exempts state employees acting within scope of employment.
The definitions chapter defines "person" (§82047), "public official" (§82048), and related terms but contains no definition of "public entity."

The lobbyist definition employs a materiality threshold ($2,000/month in compensation) and §86115(b) sets a $5,000/quarter threshold for payment-to-influence filers, effectively exempting those below the threshold from coverage.

The definition of lobbyist covers communications with "any elective state official, agency official, or legislative official" for purposes of influencing legislative or administrative action, encompassing both executive and legislative targets.

Targets include elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative officials (defined in §82038 to include legislative employees/consultants whose duties are not purely clerical), and §82037 covers the Governor's approval/veto, covering legislative branch, executive officials, and staff.

The definition covers communications with elective state officials (including the Governor), agency officials, and legislative officials for purpose of influencing legislative or administrative action.
Same as above: the statutory definition of lobbyist explicitly covers communications with elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative officials.
The definition of lobbyist covers communications with elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative officials for the purpose of influencing legislative or administrative action.

Lobbying targets per §82039 include elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative officials (which under §82038 includes legislative employees/consultants whose duties are not purely clerical/secretarial), covering legislative, executive, and staff.
The statute exempts elected public officials acting in their official capacity and state employees acting within the scope of employment from the registration provisions of the chapter.

Section 86300(a) addresses public employees and contemplates them potentially being lobbyists (capping their gifts at $10/month), and §86115(b) applies a $5,000 quarterly expenditure standard; §82039(a)(1) sets a $2,000/month compensation standard, so the law addresses public employees with compensation/expenditure thresholds.
The definitions of lobbyist, lobbying firm, and lobbyist employer rely on compensation and communication activity, not on any public charter or special government protection criterion.
The statutory definitions of lobbyist, lobbying firm, and lobbyist employer turn on compensation and communication, not on ownership criteria.
The statutory definitions do not rely on the structure or composition of revenue; they rely on compensation received and the purpose of communications with officials.
